label: Salvator Mundi

claims.value: Sold at Christie's New York, 15 November 2017, for USD 450.3 million
claims.statement: The painting was sold at Christie's New York on 15 November 2017 for 450.3 million dollars, the highest auction price recorded for a work of art.

sources.cite: Wikipedia, Salvator Mundi (Leonardo), background only, not grounds.

claims.value: Whereabouts not publicly confirmed (reported in Saudi Arabia)
claims.statement: Its current location has not been publicly confirmed; press reports place it in Saudi Arabia. Only press reports are available.

sources.cite: Wikipedia, Salvator Mundi (Leonardo), background only, not grounds.

claims.statement: Presented as Leonardo in the National Gallery, London exhibition of 2011 to 2012 and by the 2017 sale; supported by a number of specialists.

sources.cite: Wikipedia, Salvator Mundi (Leonardo), background only, not grounds.

check_in: Zöllner 2003, catalogue entry (later editions discuss it)

claims.value: Workshop or largely workshop; attribution disputed
claims.statement: Disputed by some leading specialists; others hold that the extent of restoration prevents a firm attribution. Named holders were not verified in this session.

sources.cite: Wikipedia, Salvator Mundi (Leonardo), background only, not grounds.

claims.statement: Reference works report a gap in the provenance record (Britannica: 1763 to 1900); the identification with a Salvator Mundi in the collection of Charles I is a reconstruction, not checked here.

open_questions: Every claim here rests on non admitted sources. Read Syson 2011 and the critical literature before any status change.
